public_rationale: Before the post, NewsGuard had documented an apparently AI-rewritten false story spreading online. An independent preprint also found quality deficits in Wikipedia articles detected as AI-generated. Together these support Marcus’s limited assertion of confirmation 'to some degree'. They do not establish an internet-wide net decline or the stronger possibility of Google being destroyed.
limitations: The Wikipedia study was a preprint and relied on imperfect detectors.
NewsGuard qualified its attribution of the particular rewrite to AI.
The evidence establishes specific harms, not their total prevalence or net economic impact.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: His 2023 conjecture that LLMs would be used to write garbage content undermining the internet's value has already been confirmed to some degree.

statement.excerpt: The basic conjecture then — which has already been confirmed to some degree – was that LLMs would be used to write garbage content undermining the value of the internet itself.
statement.document_title: Deep Research, Deep Bullshit, and the potential (model) collapse of science

from_speaker: already been confirmed to some degree
undermining the value of the internet itself
our_interpretation: The context dates the original conjecture to approximately February 2023. The observation concerns evidence accumulated from that period through publication on February 3, 2025.

The ordinary reading of 'to some degree' requires documented unreliable or low-quality LLM content that causes identifiable information-quality costs. It does not require a measured decline in the internet's total economic value.
'To some degree' qualifies the strength of the assertion; it is not a conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Investigations available by the post identify published LLM-generated junk and observable costs such as misleading information spreading or lower-quality reference material.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence refutes the alleged LLM attribution or information-quality harm and establishes that the asserted partial confirmation was absent during the target period.

evidence.explanation: The study examined newly created Wikipedia articles and found fewer references and weaker integration among articles flagged as AI-generated. This supports a limited deterioration in reference quality, subject to imperfect AI detection.
